input.rationale: The earlier contradiction is explained and the probe now separates the two cases reliably, so this update requests the formal execution of the fixed probe (event-bound park vs. drained control) and records the corrected pre-execution account of the question.

interpretations.rationale: Current account. Source-settled: the actor publishes each observed transition with `event_tx.send(..).await` inside `detect_and_emit_events` (actor.rs:169-199), awaited from the tick arm of the single `run` select loop (actor.rs:665-711), on the channel spawn_actor creates as async_channel::bounded(RuntimeConfig::event_capacity) (handle.rs:295-323; capacity knob handle.rs:34-35, default 1024 handle.rs:74). The handle owns a receiver from construction, so an application that ignores the event stream still leaves it unread; a Pending send there stops op.tick() (election heartbeat, resends, batch flush), incoming handling, command handling and decided-subscriber pushes, and also withholds append_notify's Timeout, which drain_notifiers would emit on the same tick path (actor.rs:201-222, contract handle.rs:114-137). Previous contradiction resolved during construction (local feedback, not receipts): the stalled-consumer variant had not frozen because the burst of proposals was decided inside a single tick gap, so only one further transition was observed and the channel never took a second send; instrumented runs showed the channel at len=1/capacity=1 with a parked actor in the no-consumer variant, and len=0 with a running actor in the burst variant. The probe is now paced (one proposal per 4ms) and reaches the bound on all three nodes at event_capacity=64, where the local runs (two consecutive, unmodified sources) show: all three channels full with live receivers, at least one actor loop parked and never answering again, its append_notify_with_timeout(300ms) unresolved after 4s, while the drained-stream control keeps all nodes answering and resolves a follower append_notify Ok(idx>=1). Defect judgment stays unresolved until the retained execution reports those comparisons; the claim under test is scoped to: a node whose client does not consume its event stream parks its actor loop once event_capacity transitions are observed, permanently losing ticks and every command reply (including the documented failure endpoints), and its participation is lost to the cluster. Counter-limitations carried forward: the trigger is client-side usage with no documented drain obligation, event_capacity only delays the parking, a dropped receiver unblocks the actor (send error ignored), no snapshot source states that a full event channel must not park the loop, and the cluster-level consequence at the default capacity (1024) is not observed by this probe.
limitations: The probe reaches the bound at event_capacity=64; it does not witness the same freeze at the default 1024, and it does not measure how many unconsumed transitions a real deployment would need.

Only the node-local consequences are asserted (command round-tripping and the append_notify endpoint); no quorum-level consequence is measured, and the parked-set is reported as `at least one node`, not as all nodes.
Local construction runs used a harness-local tokio-backed AsyncRuntime impl rather than the crate's TokioRuntime feature; the formal receipt will use the controller's clean copy.

scope.description: Bounded probe of whether an event stream the application does not consume (bounded by RuntimeConfig::event_capacity) parks the single actor loop and withholds its command/append_notify endpoints, with a drained-stream control in the same execution.
assumptions: 3 nodes, standard majority quorum, no message loss or reordering beyond the in-process transport, all nodes run in one process on one tokio runtime

event_capacity is set to 64 so the bound is reached inside a bounded window; the source-settled mechanism (send awaits whenever the channel holds event_capacity events) does not depend on the value, only the number of unconsumed transitions does

excluded: proving the cluster-wide outage (quorum loss) at the 1024 default capacity

experiment.prefix: Three real OmniPaxos instances (pid 1,2,3) are built with OmniPaxosConfig::build over omnipaxos_storage::memory_storage::MemoryStorage and driven by three real omnipaxos_runtime actors spawned with spawn_actor, using a harness-local `TestRuntime` (tokio-backed AsyncRuntime impl; the crate's TokioRuntime behind the tokio_runtime feature is not required). An in-process transport task per node forwards every message from that node's `outgoing_messages()` to the receiver returned by `msg.get_receiver()`. RuntimeConfig: tick_period 2ms, egress_period 1ms, event_capacity 64, append_notify_timeout 1500ms; ServerConfig: election_tick_timeout 3, resend_message_tick_timeout 5, batch_size 1, flush_batch_tick_timeout 100. Proposals are paced at 4ms so consecutive decided-index changes are observed in separate ticks (a burst would decide many entries inside one tick gap and produce a single amalgamated event). Case `unconsumed_event_stream_stops_actor_loop` leaves each node's event receiver unread (the handle always owns one after spawn_actor; the application never calls subscribe_events or never reads it) while ordinary appends keep the cluster busy until all three event channels are full; case `drained_event_stream_keeps_actor_loop_running` is the same cluster, capacity and activity with one difference: a task per node drains the event stream. The decisive evidence of case 1 is (a) all three event channels full with a live (not closed) receiver, (b) at least one node whose actor never answers a `decided_idx` command again across ten 200ms samples, (c) that parked node's `append_notify_with_timeout(.., 300ms)` not resolving inside 4s although the actor that would produce its Timeout runs on that same tick path; the assertion messages print the observed channel state. Case 2 requires every node to keep answering and a fresh append_notify from a follower to resolve Ok(idx>=1).

interpretations.rationale: Current account (source-only, no receipt yet): the blocking behavior itself is settled by source - detect_and_emit_events publishes every observed transition with `event_tx.send(..).await` (omnipaxos_runtime/src/actor.rs:169-199) and is awaited in the tick arm of the only actor loop (actor.rs:665-711); the event channel is bounded (RuntimeConfig::event_capacity, handle.rs:34-35, default 1024 at handle.rs:74) and subscribe_events hands out a shared receiver clone (handle.rs:254-259). With a live-but-unread receiver the send is Pending and the actor task parks, so op.tick() (which drives leader-election heartbeats, message resends and batch flushes), handle_incoming and command handling all stop; a caller then cannot even obtain the documented append_notify failure endpoint, because the Timeout is produced by drain_notifiers on that same tick path (actor.rs:201-222, contract at handle.rs:114-137). Sibling paths of the same actor were built to avoid exactly this (try_send + buffering in drain_outgoing_buf, actor.rs:232-258; try_send + defer in push_to_all_subs, actor.rs:301-333), and the crate's own regression test asserts the invariant for the outgoing channel ('must still be responsive... if flush_outgoing blocked on a full channel, this would hang', tests/async_runtime_test.rs:1040-1082). What is NOT yet established: an actual execution showing the parked loop and its consequence. A first local construction of the probe (draft/assurance_generated.rs: 3-node in-process cluster, event_capacity=1, subscribe_events() receiver retained and never read) compiled and ran, but the harness as written did not reach the expected state - no node blocked within 500ms, and even the drained-events control cluster had not decided an entry within the probe's 300ms append_notify deadline, so the cluster had presumably not yet progressed to a second observed transition/two-state leader view. Until the probe is repaired and executed through the controller, the freeze and its consequence stay unverified. Counter-limitations to carry: (a) the trigger is client-side usage (a retained but unread receiver) - the runtime documents no drain obligation, and event_capacity only delays the parking, it does not bound it; (b) a receiver that is dropped unblocks the actor (the send error is ignored), so the stall lasts exactly as long as the receiver is held; (c) no source in the snapshot states that the actor loop must stay responsive to a full event channel, so the finding rests on the contract of the handle methods (every Command-reply method, including append_notify's Timeout) plus the deliberate non-blocking design of the sibling egress paths.

Current account. Settled by source: every transition the actor observes is published with an awaited send on a channel created once in spawn_actor as async_channel::bounded(RuntimeConfig::event_capacity) (handle.rs:295-323, capacity field handle.rs:34-35, default 1024 at handle.rs:74); detect_and_emit_events issues those sends (actor.rs:169-199) and is awaited from inside the tick arm of the single run select loop (actor.rs:665-711), so a Pending send there stops op.tick(), incoming handling, command handling and decided-subscriber pushes. subscribe_events hands out a clone of that same receiver (handle.rs:254-259), and append_notify's Timeout endpoint is produced by drain_notifiers on the same tick path (actor.rs:201-222, contract handle.rs:114-137), so a parked actor would also withhold that documented failure. NOT settled: whether an unread receiver actually parks the actor. Local construction (native feedback, not retained receipts; harness draft/assurance_generated.rs) produced two contradicting observations on the same cluster shape (3 nodes, in-process transport, event_capacity=1, tick_period=2ms): (A) with no consumer task at all, i.e. only the receiver the handle itself holds, no node reached a stable leader within 10s and every current_leader() poll timed out - consistent with the park; (B) with a per-node consumer task that reads events during a healthy phase (leader elected, entries decided, all commands answered) and then stops reading while keeping the receiver (instrumented: the task confirmed it had stopped reading), the cluster went on deciding all 24 further proposals and every node kept answering commands, and a later append_notify succeeded - inconsistent with the park. Because both variants leave an unread receiver on a bounded channel, (B) defeats the currently stated premise that 'unread receiver + capacity reached => sender stays Pending'. Possible explanations not yet distinguished: the tick arm's send may not be the blocking point in (B) (e.g. produces no further events, or the send resolves immediately because the channel is closed/space exists), or (A)'s no-progress has a different cause than the one claimed. Until the decisive channel-state observation is made, the freeze and its consequence stay unverified, so no defect is asserted. Counter-limitations to carry: a dropped receiver would unblock the actor (the send error is ignored), capacity only delays the parking, no snapshot source states that the actor loop must stay responsive to a full event channel (the finding would rest on the handle-method contract plus the deliberate try_send design of the sibling egress paths), and the event_capacity=1 configuration is an extreme point of a knob whose default is 1024.
limitations: Local construction observations (harness drafts run by the agent, not controller receipts) cannot support a formal conclusion; variant (B) also used an agent-defined tokio-backed AsyncRuntime implementation rather than the crate's TokioRuntime feature.
The parked-actor consequence for the rest of the cluster (lost quorum participation) has not been observed at all, only the node-local command/append_notify endpoints.

result.summary: Requested formal execution of the repaired probe (execution_package omnipaxos_runtime, harness draft assurance_generated.rs). Resolved last turn's contradiction: the stalled-consumer variant had not frozen because a burst of proposals decided inside one tick gap produced a single amalgamated event, so the channel only ever needed one send; instrumented runs confirmed the parked loop only when a second transition followed. The harness is now paced (4ms) and reaches the bound at event_capacity=64 on all three nodes: case 1 requires all event channels full with live receivers, at least one actor permanently parked across ten samples, and its append_notify_with_timeout(300ms) unresolved after 4s; case 2 is the drained-stream control requiring all nodes responsive and a follower append_notify Ok(idx>=1). Both tests pass twice locally against the unmodified snapshot sources. Also appended an unresolved Interpretation with the corrected account and the limits (bound reached at 64 rather than the 1024 default, node-local consequences only, harness-local tokio AsyncRuntime impl). Next: interpret the retained receipt and cite its decisive parsed indices.
